mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.05), or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the statistical relationship breaks down in out-of-sample tests (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of both triggers (p > 0.10), or the interaction effect is not robust in cross-validation.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies are above their 6-month averages (p > 0.05), or the interaction is not significant in out-of-sample splits.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of extreme labor market tightness (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses in high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during prolonged housing weakness (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer spending growth.
